summary: Requests blocked after enabling region pinning (EU-only) — residency policy violations
description:
Issue summary:
Nordholm Payments enabled Hosted data residency (region pinning) to EU-only in the Console on 2025-02-21 ~09:40 PT. Immediately after enabling, production traffic began failing with deterministic residency enforcement errors.

Impact:
- ~35–60% of requests blocked for ~2 hours (spiky; correlated with model selection).
- Customer reports "sudden 409s" and inability to complete their POC transaction flows.
- Primary pain: unclear which configuration change is required (region endpoint vs allowed region set vs model availability).

Customer expectation:
- All inference and related processing stays within EU.
- If capacity is constrained, they prefer an explicit error over cross-region failover.

What we saw (customer-provided):
- HTTP status: 409
- Error code: RESIDENCY_POLICY_BLOCKED
- Message (example): "Request would be routed to us-east-1 which is not in allowed regions [eu-west-1]. Update your region pinning settings or target an allowed region endpoint."
- request_id examples: req_01HPZ7C2K7M1Z1TQ2H0Y2K3A9B, req_01HPZ7D4P8VZ6KJH9R3Q9S1W0X

Environment details:
- Hosted API
- Customer is calling via their backend service in AWS eu-central-1, but using default Redwood base URL (no explicit region in endpoint config) for part of their traffic.
- They use chat + embeddings endpoints.

Steps to reproduce (as described by customer):
1) Enable region pinning: allowed_regions = ["eu-west-1"], primary_region = "eu-west-1".
2) Send /v1/chat/completions using model redwood/llama3-70b-instruct.
3) Observe 409 policy blocks.

Initial hypothesis:
- Enforcement working as designed; requests are being evaluated for residency and blocked because routing selects a non-allowed region due to either (a) model availability, (b) client targeting a US endpoint/region implicitly, or (c) prior fallback policy now blocked.

Support questions to answer:
- Are they accidentally calling a US region endpoint / default endpoint?
- Is the requested model available in eu-west-1 for Hosted?
- Is an API key override policy set differently than org/project policy?
- Are embeddings routed differently / on a separate project?

Investigation notes (Redwood):
- Control plane check: org policy set to EU-only with allowed_regions [eu-west-1]; no cross-region fallback allowed.
- Routing traces: attempted region selection us-east-1 for llama3-70b-instruct (EU capacity/model availability constraint).
- Some embeddings requests were missing the intended project header and landed on a different project (still under same org policy, so enforcement still applies).

Customer ask:
They want to keep EU-only and need a concrete remediation checklist (client changes + what to change in allowed regions/model choice) to unblock traffic today.
comments: 2025-02-21 10:06 PT - Avery Johnson (Reporter): Customer Nordholm Payments enabled EU-only pinning and now sees 409s. They’re escalating because it blocks their POC flows. Request IDs in description. Asking for immediate guidance and whether we can safely allowlist an additional EU region.

2025-02-21 10:18 PT - Markus Klein (Assignee): Acknowledged. Looping in routing/gateway owners for quick validation of error contract + whether this is expected model availability behavior. Will provide customer-facing remediation steps ASAP.

2025-02-21 10:26 PT - Markus Klein: Quick sanity check: are they explicitly hitting an EU endpoint (eu-west) or using default base URL? If using default, they may still be routed per our global routing layer but constrained by residency. Either way, error should include the target region + allowed list; asking customer for exact payload + which model(s) fail.

2025-02-21 10:41 PT - Customer (via Avery): They are using default SDK config (no region override). Failing mostly on model redwood/llama3-70b-instruct. Embeddings failures are intermittent. They expected the platform to "just stay in EU" and pick equivalent infra there.

2025-02-21 11:03 PT - Markus Klein: Confirmed from internal traces: llama3-70b-instruct currently not available in Hosted eu-west-1 for their account tier/capacity window; router tries us-east-1 as compatible region; residency enforcement blocks (as designed). Embeddings failures appear tied to the same routing attempt when eu-west pool is saturated (router tries to fail over).

2025-02-21 11:12 PT - Markus Klein: Proposed immediate fixes (customer can pick): (1) Switch to an EU-available model variant (we can recommend redwood/llama3-8b-instruct for EU) OR (2) Expand allowed_regions to include eu-central-1 if available for their org (still EU) and set primary_region to eu-central-1 for better capacity OR (3) If they must use 70B now, Dedicated in EU or a temporary exception (not recommended) to allow us-east-1.
Also: update SDK/base URL to explicitly use EU region endpoint once configured to avoid confusion during troubleshooting.
2025-02-21 11:25 PT - Markus Klein: Asked Platform to confirm whether eu-central-1 is enabled for their org in Hosted and whether embeddings-large is deployed in eu-west-1 for their tier.

2025-02-21 12:02 PT - Sean Gallagher (SRE): Checked capacity + service map: eu-west-1 has chat pools for smaller models; 70B pool is US-only today for Hosted. Embeddings-large is in eu-west-1 but can spill under load; with pinning, spill is blocked (correct). If customer needs strict EU with higher capacity, best path is enabling eu-central-1 Hosted region for them (if available) or Dedicated EU.

2025-02-21 12:18 PT - Markus Klein: Actionable customer steps drafted:
1) In Console > Residency: add allowed region eu-central-1 (EU) if available; keep cross-region fallback disabled.
2) Update client to target EU base URL (or set region config) to reduce accidental cross-region attempts.
3) Change model to EU-supported SKU for Hosted (70B not EU-hosted yet).
4) Re-test with request_id capture and confirm 2xx.
Sending to Avery for customer comms.

2025-02-21 13:09 PT - Avery Johnson: Customer confirmed they can switch to an EU-supported model for the POC if we provide a recommended mapping. They still want a path to 70B EU for production (separate convo).

2025-02-21 13:22 PT - Markus Klein: Provided mapping guidance: for strict EU Hosted today, use redwood/llama3-8b-instruct (chat) and redwood/embeddings-large (embeddings) in eu-west-1; avoid 70B model in Hosted until EU pool is available. For larger model needs, propose Dedicated EU. Also shared error explanation: 409 indicates deterministic enforcement and no customer content was processed outside allowed regions.

2025-02-24 09:11 PT - Markus Klein: Follow-up: Customer updated model selection + pinned endpoint config to EU. Block rate dropped to near-zero; only remaining blocks were from a legacy job still requesting llama3-70b-instruct. Customer removed that path and confirmed success.

2025-02-24 09:20 PT - Markus Klein: Closing as resolved. Keeping notes for rollout: we should improve Console UX to surface "model availability by region" when pinning is enabled and include a more explicit sub-reason in the message (MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_ALLOWED_REGIONS vs generic routing-to-us-east).
resolution: Resolved with configuration + workload changes: customer switched to EU-available Hosted model(s) and updated client to target EU region explicitly. Confirmed residency enforcement behavior is correct; blocks were due to requested model/route requiring us-east-1, which is disallowed by EU-only policy.
root_cause: After enabling EU-only residency policy (allowed_regions = [eu-west-1]), the customer continued sending requests for a model (llama3-70b-instruct) that is not currently available in Hosted eu-west-1. Smart routing attempted to select us-east-1 as the compatible/available region; API gateway enforcement deterministically blocked the request with RESIDENCY_POLICY_BLOCKED (HTTP 409). A smaller set of blocks were also caused by transient EU saturation where spill/failover would have gone cross-region (now correctly blocked).
next_steps: Add/expand Console copy to highlight that region pinning may block requests when a selected model is not available in the allowed region set; recommend region-compatible models.
Product/Eng follow-up: enhance error detail to include a stable sub-code (e.g., RESIDENCY_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE) per ADR-022 guidance to reduce support load.
SE to track Nordholm’s need for 70B-in-EU as a Dedicated EU opportunity; route to Naomi Feldman / enterprise team.
